node_definition.done_when: A new tests/test_plan_edit_never_strands.py shows: with sections 2 and 3 of a fixture plan queued, editing section 3's done-when lets section 2 launch while section 3 goes held with reason plan-review-owed; the obligations view shows one row for the plan naming the held count and the review invocation; storing a review that covers section 3 releases it on the next admission pass with no coordinator call; a request held by hand stays held through that pass. The admission-time plan-review check evaluates only the request's own section and the document unit. A second test queues section 3 waiting on sections 2 and 4, with section 2 landed; narrowing the plan's waits for section 3 to section 2 alone releases it on the next pass with its stored waits rewritten by derive_wait_refs, a request dispatched with --after on an unlanded run keeps that ref through the same pass and stays awaiting-upstream, and widening section 4's waits by one unlanded section moves a queued section-4 request back to awaiting-upstream. The defect is reproduced with plan_review_gate set to enforce before the repair; the narrowed check is a parameter admit_once passes to require_plan_reviewed, and a direct dispatch keeps the whole-plan check. A third test shows a request waiting --after a run whose manifest reads blocked stays awaiting-upstream rather than blocked-upstream, and moves to blocked-upstream only for a failed or abandoned manifest or a discard. The test files importing each changed module add no failures against the base revision, measured serially as a delta with the base and head logs under the run directory; ruff check and ruff format --check pass on the changed paths.
node_definition.goal: Hold a queued request for plan review only when its own section or the document unit is uncovered, and release it when a review covers them
